mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies anticipate lower revenues.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate robust economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances with strong PAYEMS growth, or if the correlation between PAYEMS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% each within a month signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate stagflation.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint correlation between high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 1% and UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint correlation between INDPRO declines and UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
